Extra Language.notes: You can speak, read, and write one extra language of your choice.

name: Ghostwise Halfling

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Silent Speech
traits.description: You can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of you. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time.

description: Ghostwise halflings are the rarest of the hin, found only in the Chondalwood and a few other isolated forests, clustered in tight-knit clans. They are clannish and mistrustful of outsiders.

Silent Speech.notes: Can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet that shares a language, one creature at a time.

name: Tiefling Variant (Asmodeus Bloodline)

traits.name: Hellfire
traits.description: Once you reach 3rd level, you can cast the burning hands spell once per day as a 2nd-level spell. This trait replaces the hellish rebuke spell of the Infernal Legacy trait.

traits.name: Winged
traits.description: You have bat-like wings sprouting from your shoulder blades. You have a flying speed of 30 feet. This trait replaces the Infernal Legacy trait.

description: A tiefling variant descended from Asmodeus, exhibiting different qualities than standard tieflings, including hellfire magic and bat-like wings.

Hellfire.notes: Grants the ability to cast burning hands once per day as a 2nd-level spell starting at 3rd level. This trait replaces the hellish rebuke spell of the Infernal Legacy trait.

Winged.notes: Grants a flying speed of 30 feet. This trait replaces the Infernal Legacy trait.

name: Genasi

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Genasi mature at about the same rate as humans and reach adulthood in their late teens. They live somewhat longer than humans do, up to 120 years.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Independent and self-reliant, genasi tend toward a neutral alignment.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Genasi are as varied as their mortal parents but are generally built like humans, standing anywhere from 5 feet to over 6 feet tall. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Primordial. Primordial is a guttural language, filled with harsh syllables and hard consonants.

traits.name: Subraces
traits.description: Four major subraces of genasi are found among the worlds of D&D: air genasi, earth genasi, fire genasi, and water genasi. Choose one of these subraces.

subraces.name: Air Genasi

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 1.

traits.name: Unending Breath
traits.description: You can hold your breath indefinitely while you're not incapacitated.

traits.name: Mingle with the Wind
traits.description: You can cast the levitate spell once with this trait, requiring no material components, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

subraces.description: As an air genasi, you are descended from the djinn. As changeable as the weather, your moods shift from calm to wild and violent with little warning, but these storms rarely last long.

subraces.name: Earth Genasi

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Strength score increases by 1.

traits.name: Earth Walk
traits.description: You can move across difficult terrain made of earth or stone without expending extra movement.

traits.name: Merge with Stone
traits.description: You can cast the pass without trace spell once with this trait, requiring no material components, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

subraces.description: As an earth genasi, you are descended from the cruel and greedy dao, though you aren't necessarily evil. You have inherited some measure of control over earth, reveling in superior strength and solid power. You tend to avoid rash decisions, pausing long enough to consider your options before taking action.

subraces.name: Fire Genasi

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Intelligence score increases by 1.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Reach to the Blaze
traits.description: You know the produce flame cantrip. Once you reach 3rd level, you can cast the burning hands spell once with this trait as a 1st-level spell, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

subraces.description: As a fire genasi, you have inherited the volatile mood and keen mind of the efreet. You tend toward impatience and making snap judgments. Rather than hide your distinctive appearance, you exult in it.

subraces.name: Water Genasi

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Acid Resistance
traits.description: You have resistance to acid damage.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: You can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Swim
traits.description: You have a swimming speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Call to the Wave
traits.description: You know the shape water cantrip. Once you reach 3rd level, you can cast the create or destroy water spell once with this trait as a 2nd-level spell, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

subraces.description: As a water genasi, you are descended from the marids, sea chieftains known for their capriciousness. You have a natural affinity for water and can adapt to life in the sea or on land.

description: Genasi are as varied as their mortal parents but are generally built like humans, standing anywhere from 5 feet to over 6 feet tall. They are touched by elemental power, with subraces reflecting air, earth, fire, or water heritage.

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Common and Primordial.

Subraces.notes: Choose one subrace: air genasi, earth genasi, fire genasi, or water genasi.

name: Shadowborn Bearfolk

traits.name: Bite
traits.description: Your powerful jaws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If it hits, you deal 1d6 + your Strength modifier piercing damage.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.description: Your hide is thick and tough, granting you a natural AC of 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.description: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Ursine Talent
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Athletics and Perception skills.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 1.

traits.name: Cloak of Night
traits.description: While in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as though it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

description: Shadowborn bearfolk are bearfolk born in the Shadow Realm, marked by gray coats from infancy and sometimes possessing strangely arcane black markings. They resist the darkness more easily than other bearfolk and are often drawn to its presence.

Bite.notes: Natural weapon: unarmed strike dealing 1d6 + Strength modifier piercing damage.

Powerful Build.notes: Counts as one size larger for carrying capacity and push/drag/lift weight.

Cloak of Night.notes: In dim light or darkness: advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

name: Shadow Fey

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Charisma score increases by 1.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Although they have a malevolent reputation, the shadow fey are not inherently evil. They tend toward chaotic neutral, though every variation exists.

traits.name: Shadow Fey Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the rapier, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.

traits.name: Path of Shadows
traits.description: When in darkness, dim light, or a shadow large enough to cover your body, you can cast the misty step spell. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in bright sunlight.

traits.name: Traveler in Darkness
traits.description: You have advantage on any Intelligence (Arcana) check to learn about a particular shadow road and how it functions.

traits.name: Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

description: Shadow fey are a subrace of elf with skin tending toward alabaster white, ebon black, or subtle grays, and many have horns that range widely in size and shape.

Path of Shadows.notes: Can cast misty step when in darkness, dim light, or a shadow large enough to cover your body. Uses per day equal to Charisma modifier (minimum 1), regained on long rest. Charisma is the spellcasting ability.

Sunlight Sensitivity.notes: Disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight when you, the target, or the perceived object is in bright sunlight.

Traveler in Darkness.notes: Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana) checks to learn about a particular shadow road and how it functions.

Language.notes: Can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

name: Lunar Elf

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Although they have a malevolent reputation, the shadow fey are not inherently evil. They tend toward chaotic neutral, though every variation exists.

traits.name: Luminous
traits.description: You emit bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. You can choose to suppress this effect to only dim light in a 15-foot radius, to suppress it completely, or to activate it at any time without expending an action. (This effect has a level equal to your proficiency bonus, and if any of its area overlaps with an area of darkness created by a spell of the same level or lower, the spell that created the darkness is dispelled.)

traits.name: Moon Child
traits.description: When in darkness, dim light, or a shadow large enough to cover your body, you can cast the moonbeam spell. You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

traits.name: Shadow Fey Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the rapier, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in sunlight.

traits.name: Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

description: Lunar elves are identical in appearance to shadow fey except their skin glows in the dark, and they have luminous silver eyes. Their horns tend to be long, spiraled, and pearlescent.

Luminous.notes: Emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. Can suppress to dim light only, suppress completely, or activate at any time without an action. Effect has a level equal to proficiency bonus; dispels darkness spells of equal or lower level in overlapping areas.

Moon Child.notes: When in darkness, dim light, or a shadow large enough to cover your body, can cast moonbeam. Uses per day equal to Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), regained on long rest. Wisdom is the spellcasting ability.

Sunlight Sensitivity.notes: Disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight when you, your target, or what you are trying to perceive is in sunlight.

Language.notes: Can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

name: Sable Elf

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Intelligence score increases by 2, and your Dexterity decreases by 1.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Due to their exiled status, sable elves have lost attachment to many of the values traditionally held by elves. Centuries of solitude have pushed the remaining sable elves in different directions, and a variety of alignments are found within their ranks.

traits.name: Blood Affinity
traits.description: Choose a school of magic you have a natural affinity for. You learn a cantrip of your choice from that school. When you reach 3rd level, choose a 1st-level spell from the same school, and when you reach 5th level, choose a 3rd-level spell from the same school. You learn these spells and can cast them at their lowest level. Once you cast one of these spells, you must finish a long rest before you can cast the spell again using this feature. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Intelligence.

traits.name: Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

description: Sable elves are dark-eyed, often either red-haired or raven-haired, and silver-skinned. They have tall, willowy frames, similar to other elves, and most carry an irrepressible aura of world-weariness.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Intelligence score increases by 2, Dexterity decreases by 1.

Blood Affinity.notes: Choose a school of magic. Learn one cantrip from that school. At 3rd level, learn one 1st-level spell from that school; at 5th level, learn one 3rd-level spell from that school. Each spell can be cast once per long rest at its lowest level. Spellcasting ability is Intelligence.

Language.notes: Can speak, read, and write Elvish and Umbral.

name: Shadow Goblin

traits.name: Blood Affinity
traits.description: Choose a school of magic you have a natural affinity for. You learn a cantrip of your choice from that school. When you reach 3rd level, choose a 1st-level spell from the same school, and when you reach 5th level, choose a 3rd-level spell from the same school. You learn these spells and can cast them at

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Charisma score increases by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Shadow goblins reach adulthood at age 8 and can live up to 70 years.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Much like the shadow fey they coexist with, shadow goblins are not inherently evil, despite their reputations. Their natures are a constant balance between whimsy and being useful and productive. Shadow goblins are more likely to tend toward neutral good or neutral alignments.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Goblins are between 3 and 4 feet tall and weigh between 40 and 80 pounds. Your size is Small.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as though it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Quick Wit
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Deception and Insight skills.

traits.name: Shadow Camouflage
traits.description: You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in dim light or darkness.

traits.name: Stink Eye
traits.description: As an action, you can perform a combination of rude gestures and sounds to distract one creature you can see within 30 feet. If the target can hear and see you, it must make a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma ability modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failure, it has disadvantage on the next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.description: You have disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you, the target of your attack, or whatever you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

traits.name: Unseelie Blessing
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can’t put you to sleep.

traits.name: Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Goblin and Umbral.

description: Shadow goblins are blue- or purple-skinned goblins with bright orange or (text truncated) eyes, evolved to thrive in the Shadow Realm as servitors and allies of the shadow fey.

Blood Affinity.notes: Grants spellcasting: learn a cantrip from a chosen school of magic at 1st level, a 1st-level spell from that school at 3rd level, and a 3rd-level spell from that school at 5th level.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Dexterity score increases by 2, Charisma score increases by 1.

Shadow Camouflage.notes: Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in dim light or darkness.

Stink Eye.notes: Action: target one creature within 30 ft that can see and hear you; Charisma save (DC 8 + Cha mod + proficiency bonus) or have disadvantage on its next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw before the start of your next turn.

Sunlight Sensitivity.notes: Disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight when you, your target, or what you are trying to perceive is in direct sunlight.

Unseelie Blessing.notes: Advantage on saving throws against being charmed; magic can't put you to sleep.

Language.notes: Can speak, read, and write Goblin and Umbral.

name: Umbral Human

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: You may choose one score to increase by 2 and a different score to increase by 1.

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Your natural aging process slows and becomes similar to that of an elf or shadow fey.

traits.name: Alignment
traits.description: Umbral humans have often walked a troubling path to become what they are. This tends to push umbral humans toward neutral or chaotic alignments, but all variations exist.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as though it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can’t discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Dark Infusion
traits.description: You have resistance to cold damage.

traits.name: Fade Away
traits.description: While standing perfectly still, you can use an action to become invisible. You become visible again if you move or take an action. You can use this feature a number of times per day equal to your proficiency bonus.

traits.name: Language
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Common and Umbral.

traits.name: Subtypes
traits.description: The generational infusion of shadow manifests itself in different ways, but two especially noteworthy categories of umbral humans exist: changelings and the gifted. Choose one of the two subraces presented below.

subraces.name: Changeling
subraces.description: Changelings are the natural result of humans adapting to a life in the shadows over multiple generations. Originally, humans were stolen from the mortal lands to serve their shadow fey masters—or just on a whim—and many more humans simply got lost on a shadow road or abandoned and ultimately became stranded in the Shadow Realm. And that new life in shadows must ultimately change a mortal. Changelings resemble their cousins from the mortal lands but with the hallmarks of a life in the shadows, similar to how shadow fey differ from other elves. Their skin color tends toward alabaster white, ebon black, or subtle grays. Some have even grown rudimentary horns, like shadow fey. Their appearance may change further in generations to come—perhaps constantly evolving and even drastically diverging in some ways.

description: Umbral humans are humans transformed by generations of exposure to the Shadow Realm, appearing with alabaster white, ebon black, or subtle gray skin, and sometimes rudimentary horns like shadow fey.

Ability Score Increase.notes: Choose one ability score to increase by 2 and a different ability score to increase by 1.

Age.notes: Natural aging process slows to be similar to that of an elf or shadow fey.

Fade Away.notes: While standing perfectly still, can use an action to become invisible. Becomes visible again if you move or take an action. Usable a number of times per day equal to your proficiency bonus.

Language.notes: Can speak, read, and write Common and Umbral.

Subtypes.notes: Choose one of two subraces: changelings or the gifted.

name: Changeling Umbral Human

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Charisma score increases by 1.

traits.name: Cover Story
traits.description: You gain proficiency in the Deception or Persuasion skill.

traits.name: Shadow Glamour
traits.description: You can use an action to cast the disguise self spell at will.

description: Changeling umbral humans are humans adapted to the shadows, resembling their mortal cousins but with hallmarks of a life in the shadows. Their skin tends toward alabaster white, ebon black, or subtle grays, and some have even grown rudimentary horns like shadow fey.

Cover Story.notes: Gain proficiency in either Deception or Persuasion (player's choice).

Shadow Glamour.notes: Can cast disguise self at will as an action.

name: Gifted Umbral Human

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Cursed Infusion
traits.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage.

traits.name: Shadow Gift
traits.description: You struck a bargain with a shadow fey to receive a gift, but it came at a terrible price. Choose one of the options below to determine the benefit and penalty you possess (or discuss other options with your GM): • You become proficient in one skill of your choice and always roll ability checks made with that skill at advantage. Choose a second skill, and always roll ability checks made with that skill at disadvantage. • You no longer need to eat or breathe to survive and require only 4 hours for a long rest. Gain one level of exhaustion. This level of exhaustion cannot be removed by any means magical or non-magical. • Cut your current base movement speed in half. Gain a fly, swim, or climb speed equal to your newly halved base movement speed. • Increase one of your ability scores by 6 (up to 20). Reduce two different ability scores by 2. • Each day at dawn, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution score. You are no longer able to spend hit dice to heal during short rests.

description: Gifted umbral humans are broken souls—umbral humans who have drunk too deeply of the shadows, often transformed by shadow fey or dark powers. Their appearance varies widely, from seeming normal to resembling shadow fey, sometimes with tails, hooves, or vestigial wings.

Shadow Gift.notes: Choose one of the following options: (1) Proficiency in one skill of your choice with advantage on checks using it, and disadvantage on checks using a second chosen skill. (2) No need to eat or breathe; only 4 hours needed for a long rest; gain one level of exhaustion that cannot be removed by any means. (3) Base movement speed halved; gain a fly, swim, or climb speed equal to the new halved base speed. (4) Increase one ability score by 6 (max 20); reduce two different ability scores by 2. (5) Gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution score each day at dawn; cannot spend hit dice to heal during short rests.

name: Wyrd Gnome

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Natural Diviner
traits.description: You have an innate knack for understanding the world and can catch glimpses of the mysteries of the universe. You know the guidance cantrip. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the identify spell with this trait, requiring no material components, and starting at 5th level, you can cast the augury spell with it. Once you cast a non-cantrip spell with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Prescience
traits.description: When you finish a long rest, roll a d20 and record the number rolled. Before your next long rest, you can replace one attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature that you can see with this prescience roll. You must choose to do so before the roll. If 20 wyrd gnomes are present within a half mile of you when you make the prescience roll, you can add 1 to the result. Every time the number of nearby wyrd gnomes is doubled, you gain an additional bonus of 1 to the roll (+2 for 40 gnomes, +3 for 80, and so on) to a maximum bonus of +5.

description: Wyrd gnomes are gnomes with a natural prescience that sets them apart from most other gnomes. They have gathered together in small communities of their own kind over generations.

Natural Diviner.notes: Knows the guidance cantrip. At 3rd level can cast identify (no material components) once per long rest. At 5th level can cast augury once per long rest. Wisdom is the spellcasting ability for these spells.

Prescience.notes: After a long rest, roll a d20 and record it. Before the next long rest, can replace one attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature you can see with this roll (must decide before the roll). Bonus to the prescience roll based on nearby wyrd gnomes: +1 if 20 within half a mile, +1 per doubling (max +5).

name: Dwarves of the Iron Hills

traits.name: Ability Score Increases
traits.description: Your Constitution and Strength scores increase by 2.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 50 to 100. Dwarves generally start their life on the road in their fifties, and do not usually consider retiring before their nineties. Around that time, they feel they can no longer stay away from their family, or want to dedicate themselves solely to the perfection of their crafts. But Dwarves can remain active until they are more than two hundred years old, and may return to adventuring if a great need arises, like the opportunity to avenge an old insult or injury, or to recover a treasure or reclaim a long-lost dwarf-hold. A healthy Dwarf who avoids a violent death can reach two hundred fifty years of age.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Dwarves generally stand between 4 to 5 feet tall and can weigh upwards of 160 lbs. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 ft. Your speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

traits.name: Night Vision (Dwarf)
traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 ft of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Tools for War
traits.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, mattocks and warhammers.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan’s tools of your choice: jeweller’s tools, mason’s tools, miner’s tools, smith’s tools, or woodcarver’s tools. You also gain proficiency in one musical instrument of your choice.

traits.name: Stonecunning
traits.description: Whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check related to the origin of stonework, you are considered proficient in the History skill and add double your Proficiency Bonus to the check, instead of your normal Proficiency Bonus.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

traits.name: Sworn Allegiance
traits.description: "We are hastening to our kinsmen in the Mountain, since we learn that the kingdom of old is renewed." Your do not give your trust to others easily, but when it happens, the bond that is formed is so strong that you treat your friends as kinsmen. The first time that you complete a long rest during an Adventuring phase you gain Inspiration as long as your companions are not Paralysed, Petrified, Poisoned, Miserable, Stunned or Unconscious. If at least half of the Company are Dwarves, you gain Inspiration in this manner after each long rest, not just the first one.

traits.name: Ironfoot Hauberk (Ring-mail)
traits.description: The ancient weaponsmiths of your folk possessed the secret of forging a hauberk of steel mail, made of a fine and flexible mesh that is especially comfortable and lightweight (for a suit of metal armour). You do not have Disadvantage on Stealth checks when wearing the Ironfoot Hauberk. Furthermore, if you have Dexterity of 12 or higher, the armour provides AC 15.

description: The Dwarves of the Iron Hills are a hardy breed of Dwarves who live the simple but harsh life of miners and smiths, often gruff and terse with outsiders. They sport long, forked beards, plaited and thrust into their belts when they travel, fight or work the forge.

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor

Night Vision (Dwarf).notes: Can see in dim light within 60 ft as if it were bright light, but cannot see in darkness (not darkvision)

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison

Stonecunning.notes: Considered proficient in History for Intelligence (History) checks related to origin of stonework, and adds double proficiency bonus instead of normal proficiency bonus

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Dalish and the secret language of the dwarves

Sworn Allegiance.notes: Gain Inspiration after first long rest during an Adventuring phase if companions are not Paralysed, Petrified, Poisoned, Miserable, Stunned, or Unconscious; if at least half the Company are Dwarves, gain Inspiration after each long rest

Ironfoot Hauberk (Ring-mail).notes: No disadvantage on Stealth checks when wearing Ironfoot Hauberk; if Dexterity is 12 or higher, the armor provides AC 15

traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2 and your Wisdom increases by 1.

traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 ft of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Tools for War
traits.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes, great axes, hammers, and mattocks.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency

traits.name: Born to the Road
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Survival skill. When beginning a journey where you serve as Guide for the Company, you may spend Inspiration instead of making an Embarkation Roll. You may choose one of the following results: Fine Weather, Paths Both Swift and True or Hidden from the Shadow.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Dalish, which is the tongue of the Bardings, who speak an older version of the Common Tongue. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

description: Dwarves of the Grey Mountains are a sturdy folk of stone and iron, dwelling in the cold halls beneath the Grey Mountains. They are known for their craftsmanship, resilience, and deep grudges.

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor

name: Dwarf of the Blue Mountains

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Constitution score increases by 2.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 50 to 100. Dwarves generally start their life on the road in their fifties, and do not usually consider retiring before their nineties. Around that time, they feel they can no longer stay away from their family, or want to dedicate themselves solely to the perfection of their crafts. But Dwarves can remain active until they are more than two hundred years old, and may return to adventuring if a great need arises, like the opportunity to avenge an old insult or injury, or to recover a treasure or reclaim a long-lost dwarf-hold. A healthy Dwarf who avoids a violent death can reach 250 years of age.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Dwarves generally stand between 4 to 5 feet tall and can weigh upwards of 160 lbs. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 feet. Your speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armour.

traits.name: Night Vision (Dwarf)
traits.description: Accustomed to life underground, you have superior vision in dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, but you cannot see in the dark.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Weapons of the Trade
traits.description: You have proficiency with axes, hand-axes and mattocks.

traits.name: Tool Proficiency
traits.description: You gain proficiency with the artisan's tools of your choice: jeweller's tools, mason's tools, miner's tools, smith's tools, or woodcarver's tools. You also gain proficiency in one musical instrument of your choice.

traits.name: Singer of the Old Songs
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Performance skill.

traits.name: Tales of Days Gone By
traits.description: You have proficiency in either the History or Lore skill (your choice) and increase your Intelligence score by 1.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write Westron, the Common Tongue of Eriador. You can also speak, read and write the secret language of your people, which has never been shared with any others.

description: An extraordinarily venerable Dwarf of the Blue Mountains, Iari has decided that he wishes to see the restored Kingdom Under the Mountain before he dies.

Speed.notes: Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor.

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison.

Tool Proficiency.notes: Choose one artisan's tools from the listed options; also gain proficiency in one musical instrument of choice.

Tales of Days Gone By.notes: Choose either History or Lore skill proficiency; Intelligence score increases by 1.

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Westron (Common Tongue of Eriador) and the secret dwarven language.

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Dalish.

name: Dwarves of the Lonely Mountain

traits.name: Dwarven Combat Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against poison, and you have resistance against poison damage.

traits.name: Dwarven Toughness

traits.name: Night Vision
traits.description: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Road Wisdom
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Survival skill.

description: Dwarves of the Lonely Mountain are sturdy and resilient, with thick beards and a strong connection to their ancestral home of Erebor.

Dwarven Resilience.notes: Advantage on saving throws against poison

name: Mirkwood Elf

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2 and your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 100 to 500. Elves are invulnerable to age, and may become adventurers at any time after they reach adulthood (at about a century of age). Considering the level of ability of a starting hero, players should avoid choosing an excessively venerable age for their character.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Elves range from 5 to over 6 feet tall, with slender builds. Your size is Medium.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

traits.name: Night Vision
traits.description: Accustomed to twilight forests and the night sky, you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light.

traits.name: The Eyes of Elves
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Perception skill.

traits.name: Elvish Dreams
traits.description: Your sleep is not like that of mortals. When you sleep, you can choose to send your mind into an “Elvish Dream” retaining full consciousness of your surroundings and you needn’t close your eyes. Four hours spent in such dreams acts on you as if you had rested an entire night.

traits.name: The Tools of War
traits.description: You have proficiency with daggers, spears, broadswords, short swords, and short bows.

traits.name: A Whisper Through the Leaves
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Stealth skill. You have advantage on Stealth skill checks whenever you are in a forest and can make Hide attempts even when only lightly obscured by foliage.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak the old language of your people, the Woodland tongue, along with the ability to speak, read, and write Sindarin. You can also speak the Common Tongue.

description: Mirkwood Elves are slender, tall Elves ranging from 5 to over 6 feet, accustomed to twilight forests and the night sky, and are staunch fighters dedicated to resisting the encroaching darkness.

Elvish Dreams.notes: Can retain full consciousness of surroundings while sleeping; 4 hours of Elvish Dream counts as a full night's rest.

A Whisper Through the Leaves.notes: Advantage on Stealth checks in forests; can attempt to hide when only lightly obscured by foliage.

Languages.notes: Can speak Woodland tongue, Sindarin (speak/read/write), and Common.

name: Hobbit

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 25-60. Hobbits do not easily abandon their comfortable lives, but when they do they usually wait at least for their coming of age at 33. But a particularly reckless Hobbit might feel the call to adventure when in his tweens, as Hobbits call their twenties. Hobbits generally pass early in their second century, remaining fairly healthy until the very end of their twilight years.

traits.name: Size
traits.description: Hobbits are generally just slightly under three feet tall and weigh around 50 lbs. Your size is Small.

traits.name: Speed
traits.description: Your base walking speed is 25 feet.

traits.name: Resilient
traits.description: You have advantage on saving throws against Corruption.

traits.name: Hobbit Nimbleness
traits.description: You can move through the space of any creature who is at least one size larger than yours.

traits.name: Noble Pursuits
traits.description: You have proficiency with short bows. You gain proficiency with one artisan’s tool of your choice: brewer’s supplies, carpenter’s tools, cartographer’s tools, cook’s utensils, gardener’s tools, potter’s tools, smith’s tools, weaver’s tools, or woodcarver’s tools. You also gain proficiency with pipes.

traits.name: Hobbit Elusiveness
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Stealth skill.

traits.name: Languages
traits.description: You can speak, read, and write the Common Tongue, or Westron as the scholars have it. Whatever native tongue the Hobbits once had is all but gone, save for a few unique words such as “mathom” – an object one has no immediate use for, but for whatever reason, is unwilling to throw away.

subraces.name: Harfoot

traits.name: Unobtrusive
traits.description: You can attempt to hide even when you are obscured only by a creature that is at least one size larger than you.

subraces.description: Harfoot family line of Hobbits.

subraces.name: Stoor
subraces.description: Stoor family line of Hobbits.

Hobbit Nimbleness.notes: Can move through the space of any creature at least one size larger.

Noble Pursuits.notes: Proficiency with short bows; proficiency with one artisan's tool of choice from the listed options; proficiency with pipes.

Languages.notes: Can speak, read, and write Common (Westron).

traits.description: Your Intelligence score increases by 1.

traits.name: Student of Old Lore
traits.description: You have proficiency in the Lore skill and with calligrapher's supplies.

description: Fallowhides are a family line of Hobbits, one of the three original breeds, known for their scholarly pursuits and interest in old lore.

They may become adventurers any time after they reach adulthood, although they are unlikely to venture beyond Imladris until they are half a millennia or more old. Even though a starting High Elf is far more 'experienced' than those of other cultures, he is still young and weak compared to his elder kin, and so is unlikely to be more than a thousand years old.

traits.name: Adventuring Age
traits.description: 16-30. Those of Firienseld don't usually venture far from the Burg until their 16th year and rarely continue past their fortieth year, when the desire to return to the mountains of their youth becomes strong.

traits.description: Your Dexterity score increases by 2 and you may increase any two other ability scores by 1.

Those who venture out are either young and taking desperate chances or have had some calamity foisted upon them. Around their fiftieth year, even the most ambitious Wild Hobbits think seriously of finding a hidden refuge and attending to their family's needs.

traits.name: Speed

traits.description: You have proficiency with the longbow, shortbow, and all simple weapons.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry

traits.description: Elves don't need to sleep. Instead, they meditate deeply, remaining semiconscious, for 4 hours a day. (The Common word for such meditation is "trance.") While meditating, you can dream after a fashion; such dreams are actually mental exercises that have become reflexive through years of practice. After resting in this way, you gain the same benefit that a human does from 8 hours of sleep.

traits.name: Windrunner Weapon Training
traits.description: You have proficiency with the windrunner bolas, windrunner boomerang, and birding shaft.

traits.name: Kitecraft
traits.description: You have proficiency with kites and can use them to cross chasms and other treacherous land, launch from horseback, or descend from precipices. You can also use kites for competitive events, herding livestock, and marking land for grazing and water.

description: Elusive, eccentric, and unpredictable, windrunner elves have quietly traversed Midgard's vast central grasslands for millennia. These diminutive nomads roaming the steppes and plains are thought to originally hail from the elven capital of Sephaya, long since abandoned during the Great Retreat.

Fey Ancestry.notes: Advantage on saving throws against being charmed; magic can't put you to sleep.

Trance.notes: Don't need to sleep; meditate 4 hours for benefits of 8 hours of sleep.

Kitecraft.notes: Can use kites to cross chasms, launch from horseback, descend precipices, and for competitive events, herding livestock, and marking land.

name: Winterfolk Halfling

traits.name: Coldforged Tools
traits.description: Winterfolk metalworking is done at low temperatures and most communities have at least one member capable of creating masterful coldforged items. Tools crafted by the winterfolk serve double duty as weapons as well.

traits.name: Tool Weapons
traits.description: Many of the tools forged by the winterfolk can be used as weapons by simply substituting the closest approximation. A trowel acts as a dagger, a spade acts as a battleaxe, and a pitchfork acts as a trident, for instance.

description: Winterfolk halflings are a reclusive, rugged people who dwell in the northern Rothenian Plains, hiding in small communities of sod-roofed huts. They are superstitious, hardy, and value privacy and community above all.

Coldforged Tools.notes: Flavor trait about crafting coldforged items; no direct mechanical effects.

Tool Weapons.notes: Allows tools to be used as equivalent weapons (trowel=dagger, spade=battleaxe, pitchfork=trident); no proficiency granted by this trait itself.

name: Riverfolk Halfling

traits.name: Sure-Footed
traits.description: You're tough and strong despite your small size, no stranger to hard work, labor, and working muscle against the will of a river. Your Strength score is increased by 1. Additionally, you are adept at maintaining your balance on wet decks; you have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to keep your balance. Slippery surfaces are not considered difficult terrain for you.

traits.name: River's Child
traits.description: You have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to swim. Additionally, you add twice your Wisdom bonus on your Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks with advantage if the animal is native to rivers or nests in riverbanks. You can sense ley lines that cross or run parallel to a river within 1 mile of you but gain no other benefit to tap into or unlock it.

description: Riverfolk are city halflings, usually growing up on docks, fishing boats, and the patchwork barges. Most are more at home on a temperamental river than on solid ground, and riverfolk seldom fear drowning.

Sure-Footed.notes: Strength score increased by 1. Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks to keep balance. Slippery surfaces are not difficult terrain.

River's Child.notes: Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to swim. Adds twice Wisdom bonus on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks with advantage for river-native animals. Can sense ley lines within 1 mile of a river.

name: Courtfolk

traits.name: Fey-Touched Finery
traits.description: Courtfolk are as small in size and stature as any halfling. Their long proximity to elves and the Elflands shows in their complexion, usually pale and freckled with light-colored eyes and curly mops of hair. Courtfolk prefer neat, well-tailored clothing (most of which they make themselves) with touches of elven inspiration apparent without ever descending into gaudy imitation. Men typically wear baggy trousers and tight vests and women favor flowing skirts with bodices. Colors are pastel or forest tones and muted, befitting a servant, but never drab. Elven jewelry is common among halflings of any gender as are smoking pipes. Courtfolk women particularly favor pipes of unique design.

traits.name: History of Servitude
traits.description: The provenance of the courtfolk—indeed, all halflings—is the subject of speculation, and one the halflings themselves are curiously unconcerned with solving. Some suspicious humans maintain halflings were once human servants, but frequent exposure to the Elflands and the magic there left them stunted and enthralled to the fey. An occasional mage postulates the halflings were wholly created as elven servitors, made up partly of Midgard's substance and given life by fey magic. The courtfolk themselves laugh off such claims. They maintain they are simply halflings, but unlike the reclusive winterfolk and sly riverfolk, they did not break faith with the covenant they forged, by choice, with the great elven lords and ladies of old. The courtfolk are what halflings should be, they claim, and their pitiable offshoot cousins are defined by their loss of purpose. Numerous families of courtfolk once served elven courts from Arbonesse to Valera and every holding in between. They were expert craftsmen, faithful seneschals, discreet handmaids, efficient butlers, reliable messengers, unexpected bodyguards, and talented gardeners such that their elven masters trusted few others with their breathtaking gardens and courtyards. While never ostentatious, halflings whose families served since the earliest days of the elves' arrival bore a certain prestige among their own, respect owed for the lengths of their good service. Most of these families disappeared in the Great Retreat with their lords and ladies, separated from friends and kin. Those remaining behind honored their oaths, lingering in the fading courts and subservient to elfmarked descendants of once-mighty rulers. Time wore on, and a seed of sorrow took root in the courtfolk, though hidden by deference and cheery service. The names of kin gone since the Last Horn are recorded among them from generation to generation and repeated in their private songs and stories.

traits.name: Servants Without Masters
traits.description: Courtfolk enjoy long lives, lingering in a pleasant old age for up to 350 years, a century longer than most halflings do. Most have a parent or grandparent who remembers the old courts and passed down their stories, mannerisms, and a keen sense of loss. As such, adapting to newfound freedom in only one or two generations has proven difficult for those who remained after the Last Horn. As observed with some small bitterness, those halflings who abandoned their duties and wandered away, becoming winterfolk and riverfolk elsewhere, seem to have had less trouble. description: Courtfolk are a halfling subrace with obvious elven influence, mired as they have been in elven culture for generations. They are at home in elven courts and politics, with a soft and lilting flair to their names and an innate glamour.

Fey-Touched Finery.notes: Purely descriptive/flavor trait. No mechanical effects.

History of Servitude.notes: Purely descriptive/flavor trait. No mechanical effects.

Servants Without Masters.notes: Descriptive trait noting a lifespan of up to 350 years. No direct combat or proficiency mechanics.

name: Courtfolk Halfling

traits.name: Age
traits.description: Courtfolk are the longest-lived of the halfling subraces, perhaps owing to their close association with elves. Courtfolk are elderly by their second century but enjoy relatively pleasant and unhindered old age well past 300 years.

traits.name: Boon Companion
traits.description: You are  quick to step in and help your friends, and you have a knack for knowing exactly how to best do it. When you work with an ally to complete a task or take the Help action in combat, your ally adds a d4 to their check or attack roll (this includes the second roll made with advantage).

traits.name: Wee Glamour
traits.description: You are—ever so slightly—imbued with a bit of elven magic. You move with grace, your laugh is always pleasant, and colors are more vibrant on you. Your Charisma score increases by 1, and you have advantage on saves against spells of the enchantment school.

subraces.name: Variant Courtfolk: Shadow Servitors

traits.name: Disquiet
traits.description: You still look like your old self, but your mind is changed by the knowledge you’ve accepted—and you’re not sure it’s for the better. Your Intelligence score increases by 1. Additionally, something in your eyes makes people uneasy around you. You have advantage on Charisma (Intimidate) and Charisma (Deception) checks against humanoids.

traits.name: Silent Steps
traits.description: You’ve always been adept at evading notice, but now your own shadow seems to muffle the noise you make. You can cast the silence spell once per day centered on yourself, which you can end at any time by speaking. Additionally, you always have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to be quiet.

subraces.description: Those courtfolk who elect to serve shadow fey are usually broken spirits to start with, and over time, the cracks in their souls become filled with something darker.

description: Courtfolk halflings are a subrace of halflings who have lived in elven courts for generations, developing a graceful and unobtrusive demeanor. They have a soft, lilting flair to their names and a deep connection to elven culture and magic.

Age.notes: Flavor trait only; no mechanical effects.

Boon Companion.notes: When you work with an ally to complete a task or take the Help action in combat, your ally adds a d4 to their check or attack roll (including the second roll made with advantage).

Wee Glamour.notes: Charisma score increases by 1. Advantage on saving throws against spells of the enchantment school.
